winner.title: Plain Sadza (Zimbabwean Mealie-Meal Porridge)

evidence.authenticity: Zimbabwean author; traditional cold-water paste then boiling water, then add meal in stages; uses Shona terms (rakukwata, mona sadza); notes refined vs unrefined (mugaiwa) meal.
evidence.precision: 7 scoops (about 50 g each per author comment), 1 cup cold water, 750 ml boiling water; cues: full boil, smooth not grainy; no pan size; thickness left to preference.
evidence.testing: Each step has a stated reason (lumps, cooking through, control of thickness); troubleshooting for grainy texture in author notes. Home cook, not a test kitchen.
evidence.photos: Pictorial steps: lettered photos for steps 1 and 3, step 2 photos, plus finished shot (confirmed via WebFetch).
evidence.access: Needs white maize meal (mealie-meal); no US substitute given, though fine white cornmeal or maize flour from US grocery or African/Latin markets works.

winner.why: It is the only candidate for the first-named component (sadza) with a Zimbabwean author, stated reasons per step and process photos; the others were Westernized or lacked cues.

runnerUp.title: Sadza Nenyama (Beef and Kale Stew)

evidence.authenticity: Covers both sadza and stew in one recipe with background, but uses kale, yellow cornmeal, butter, chili flakes and garlic powder; Westernized.
evidence.precision: US volumes, times per step, only 'large pot'; doneness cues limited to 'tender' and 'firm enough to shape'; no weights.
evidence.testing: Little explanation of why; no ratings.
evidence.access: Royco Usavi is optional with a spice-blend substitute.

runnerUp.why: Only single-page full dish, but adapted and less precise than the ZimboKitchen pair.

companions.title: Traditional Zimbabwean Beef Stew
companions.why: Authentic everyday Zimbabwean relish with 600 g beef and 3 stages of photos, but vague onion and tomato sizes and no tenderness time; soup powder needs a sub (Royco or stock cube plus cornstarch from comments).
